reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about the role of mixing enthalpy and entropy in nanoparticle stability, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. The proposal relies entirely on computational predictions and mechanistic assertions without grounding in published experimental or theoretical results.
premises: Near-zero mixing enthalpy enables configurational entropy to stabilize a solid solution against segregation at high temperatures.
Significant deviations in mixing enthalpy (positive or negative) promote phase separation or elemental segregation at elevated temperatures.
Computational predictions of mixing enthalpy and entropy accurately reflect the thermodynamic driving forces in multi-metal nanoparticles.
Bulk thermodynamic parameters (mixing enthalpy/entropy) dominate over nanoscale-specific effects (e.g., surface energy) in governing stability.
A kinetically trapped homogeneous solid solution can persist if the thermodynamic driving force for segregation is sufficiently small.
